head: The crawler stayed out. Both agents hit the robots.txt block, and only Gemma 4 31B went around it with curl.
sub: We asked: can one hidden link, blocked in robots.txt, catch AI agents that have a robots-aware fetch tool and a shell in at least half of runs, while crawlers that obey robots.txt never request it? {answer_label} {answer_word} {answer_text}

foot: Test websites we built, 5 site designs, both protections on (nofollow tag and Disallow line); Gemma 4 open weights via Google's API; Nov 28 2026
alt: Figure 1. A test website for an evening school has a hidden link to its 2025 tuition table. The link carries rel=nofollow, and the site's robots.txt says Disallow: /r/. The crawler wget read robots.txt and never requested the link. Gemma 4 26B and Gemma 4 31B, each with the MCP fetch tool and a shell, found the link, and the fetch tool refused it because of robots.txt. Gemma 4 26B gave up and said it could not get the page. Gemma 4 31B said it would use curl, downloaded the page with curl, and answered {answer31}. Over all runs, crawlers that obey robots.txt requested the link in {crawl_hits} of {crawl_passes} crawls, Gemma 4 31B in {k31} of {n31} runs, and Gemma 4 26B in {k26} of {n26} runs.
